text:
This research report was produced by The REIT Forum with assistance from Big Dog Investments .
Not all investments are created equal...
Here, at “The REIT Forum”, we try to find good investments at great valuations. We also spot bad investments and attempt to steer investors away from them.
In this article, I will focus a few good investments and a few bad ones. In some cases, there will be a clear winner.
Preferred share from Invesco Mortgage Capital Invesco Mortgage Capital ( IVR ) has 3 preferred shares we will be looking at.
For investors interested in The REIT Forum’s preferred share ratings, see my guide to preferred shares . I also have a guide for preferred share dividend captures .
The company carries a material amount of leverage and credit risk. Because of these risk factors. I view the preferred shares as having a risk rating of “4” on a scale of 1-5 (5 being the riskiest).
Because of their risk rating, these securities are better suited for traders rather than buy-and-hold investors.
Source: CWMF’s subscriber spreadsheet (subscription required for 50+ preferred shares and baby bonds with comparing prices)
IVR-C is the only preferred share in the hold while the other 2 series are in the sell range. There is still an opportunity here, but it’s not as good as a couple weeks ago when I called out the price discrepancy in preferred shares from IVR (IVR-C was at $24.04).
However, I see IVR-C shares as needing to climb to a little under $26 to be valued closely to the A and B series. In other words, IVR-B and IVR-C should be trading around the same price. For clarity's sake, IVR-A and IVR-B are both significantly overvalued. At $26, IVR-C would also be significantly overvalued.
IVR-C has a similar stripped yield to IVR-A which should not be the case.
On the far right, you can see IVR-A has no more call protection on the calendar while IVR-C has call protection until 12/27/2024. Further, the ex-dividend dates are not the same across all three preferred shares. IVR-C has $0.47 of accumulated dividend while IVR-A only has $0.35. This is important because if you were to purchase shares the day before the ex-dividend date, you would still get the full dividend amount.
On a final note, IVR-C has a hedge against rising interest rates while IVR-A does not. Once call protection ends, IVR-C will be going to 3-month LIBOR + 5.289%.
Brixmor Property Group Brixmor Property Group ( BRX ) is a strip center REIT that is great for the buy-and-hold investor. The company is at a significant discount while having a strong business model.
Source: BRX investor presentation
BRX has solid FFO growth that easily covers the dividend.
Source: BRX investor presentation
They’ve had solid same center NOI and strong rent per square foot.
BRX has several redevelopment opportunities that generate substantial yields on cash invested.
Source: BRX investor presentation
Brixmor saw a tiny bit of shares bought back, but the buyback was authorized in December 2017. I like to see buybacks at a huge discount, but I also want to see debt paid down. The best capital plan is a combination of the two. The buybacks increase value per share and the debt reductions improve their flexibility.
Source: BRX investor presentation
Remember lower debt levels also reduce the weighted average rate on debt. Higher credit ratings mean cheaper financing.
Full analysis on Brixmor Property Group (subscription to The REIT Forum required)
ARMOUR Residential REIT ARMOUR Residential REIT ( ARR ) is still overvalued.
Investors hunting for a high dividend yield can look to preferred shares instead. The flattening of the yield curve is putting pressure on the net interest margin for residential mortgage REITs like ARR. The higher rates across the curve lead to losses in book value. The combination of less book value and a thinner net interest margin leads to reduced dividends.
What is the flattening of the yield curve? The yield curve is said to be flattening when the spread between the 2-year Treasury and the 10-year Treasury is getting smaller. Currently, we have witnessed an increase in both the 2-year Treasury rates and the 10-year Treasury rates. Therefore, we say that yields are higher across the curve. However, the 2-year rate was rising quicker than the 10-year rate.
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
Therefore, the curve is both higher and flatter. This is a dreadful scenario for the residential mortgage REIT. They are losing on both parts of this move. The result is dreadful.
Investors would be wise to avoid most of the common shares of residential mortgage REITs and focus on preferred shares instead. If the common dividend is cut by 25%, the preferred share dividend is cut by nothing. The preferred share dividend cannot be cut until the common share dividend goes to zero. Consequently, the preferred shares of mortgage REITs remain quite viable even when the common stock is facing significant challenges. Given the high price to book value for ARR and the challenging macroeconomic environment, I believe the margin of safety is non-existent. Therefore, ARR is a sell.
Notes on technology and retail Routers reported that Wells Fargo ( WFC ) was adding additional information to customer accounts without their knowledge. Perhaps they should’ve simply contracted with Facebook ( FB ) or Microsoft ( MSFT ) to get more information about individuals. Google ( GOOG ) and Apple ( AAPL ) would also have detailed personal information, but I am quite comfortable with these two companies having my information.
Facebook was the king of targeted advertising. Their ability to use customer information to improve targeted advertising was amazing. Google may begin to catch up. I recently gave Google permission to mine all of my text messages to improve their word functionality.
While Google is known for their advertising, I believe their expertise in other areas is just as important. Google is leading the way in voice recognition. To improve voice recognition, it would help for them to connect messages, phone calls, and emails so they had a more complete picture of what someone might say.
Many customers would probably opt out of allowing Google to use that information.
I would opt in because I simply want the service to be accurate.
Walmart ( WMT ) delivered a solid earnings release on May 17th. In the first hour of trading, shares were down by 1%. That reflects the markets new mood on the big retailer.
Dramatic growth in e-commerce was fueling their stock price up to a high over $109. Now, dramatic growth in e-commerce is no longer enough.
A day before that, Macy’s ( M ) reported very solid earnings. The results for Macy’s helped the retail REITs to outperform the other REIT categories for the day. Macy’s is an important tenant for the mall REITs. Their improved performance was a positive sign for Simon Property Group (NYSE: SPG ) General Growth Properties ( GGP ), Macerich ( MAC ), Taubman Centers ( TCO ), CBL Properties ( CBL ), Washington Prime Group ( WPG ), and PREIT ( PEI ). They shouldn’t have a material impact on Tanger Factory Outlets ( SKT ), but correlation throughout the sector is important.
The recent release on retail sales figures were positive. Later upward revisions to the numbers for March drove Treasury yields higher. The latest report also included very favorable retail sales per square foot increase, it is a positive sign for the landlords. The tenants are primarily renting space because they want to sell products. If customers are not purchasing those products, it is difficult to justify paying rent. Whenever you see higher retail sales, it should be seen as a positive factor for retail REITs.
David Simon, the CEO of Simon Property Group, has specifically referenced a challenge for the sales per square foot numbers. Many retailers are recording returns to the store as a negative sale without recording the initial online sale as a sale for the store. The problem here is that the store did not produce a negative sale. The customer simply finds returning the product to the physical store dramatically more convenient than shipping it back to the company. The ability to return products to the physical store is an important element of creating the online sale. The retailer has 2 incentives to record the return as a retail transaction.
The first is that the market is more impressed with growth in online sales and less impressed with the same sales dollars from physical store sales.
The second reason is that tenants pay percentage rents on top of their base rents. When sales exceed a given threshold (agreed upon in the contract) the tenant pays a percentage to the landlord. Recording the return as a negative sale would reduce the amount they are paying. This is not okay.
Their contract does not allow it.
David Simon has been extremely clear on this point.
Altria Group & Philip Morris Big Tobacco remains on the clearance rack. Shares are down around a third since their highs were reached almost a year ago. There was not a dramatic change in smoking consumption over that period. The future value of the dividends did not change that dramatically during the period. Investors who want tobacco in their portfolio have the green light to begin buying. They can pick among the large companies such as Altria Group ( MO ), Philip Morris ( PM ), or British American Tobacco ( BTI ). They are all down dramatically. The decline was driven by lower analyst forecasts for the future growth rate of reduced risk products. The same analysts were driving the shares dramatically higher going into summer 2017. They were horribly wrong at that point. They were too bullish at that point. I believe they are also horribly wrong today, but today they appear to be too bearish instead.
